title: Astrid and the Ledger
premise: In 1890s Broome, Gideon Eriksen, a pearl diver's daughter indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, has learned that survival means silence. When an abandoned child is left at her door clutching a ledger that documents the company's trafficking in indentured divers, Gideon becomes the unwilling keeper of proof that could hang her own masters — and free hundreds like her. Smuggling the ledger past three checkpoints with the help of a conflicted customs officer she comes to love, she loses allies, nearly loses the child, and finally chooses justice over safety, testifying at ruinous cost and walking out of the courtroom into an uncertain but unowned life.
about_author: Coral Thornbury is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing pearling industry records along the northwest coast. Her fiction draws on the ledgers, letters, and silences she found in those boxes.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. We meet her at nineteen, diving for shells under Meridian contract, counting breaths and keeping her head down. A flashback establishes her father's death in company waters and why she never makes trouble. Emotional beat: weary endurance mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: A Bundle on the Step
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. During a storm, a toddler is left at her barracks door with a note: forget the face. Wrapped in the child's blanket is a slim ledger of names, dates, and payments. Gideon recognizes the handwriting as her late father's. Beat: fear cracking open curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, night scenes. By candlelight she deciphers entries: bribes to inspectors, deaths recorded as 'losses,' children sold between stations. She realizes the child may be the daughter of a diver who tried to testify. Beat: horror hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Man from Customs
chapters.summary: Elias Ward's POV. Customs officer Elias Ward inspects the station and notices Gideon watching him too carefully. Their first exchange is wary, almost adversarial — he suspects everyone; she must not be suspected. Beat: two sharp minds circling.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Gate
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The ledger must reach a magistrate in town before the quarterly audit destroys loose papers. Gideon sews pages into her diving suit lining and passes the station gate where the overseer searches women at random. Beat: cold terror, first small victory.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The toddler, whom she names Nell, says a word that matches a name in the ledger. Gideon understands Nell herself is living evidence. Hiding her becomes harder. Beat: tenderness entangling duty.

chapters.title: Elias's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias finds an anomaly in shipping manifests and begins his own quiet investigation, unaware Gideon holds the key. He recalls his father, ruined for challenging a company once. Beat: ambition wrestling conscience.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A fellow diver, Sefu, guesses what she carries and offers help — then someone reports a 'suspicious bundle' to the overseer. Gideon moves the ledger to a cache in the shell heaps. Beat: trust and betrayal in the same breath.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Jetty
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Gideon attempts to pass the ledger by boat to a sympathetic nun; Elias is assigned to search the jetty the same morning. He lets her pass without knowing why — or does he? Beat: charged ambiguity, near discovery.

chapters.title: What Elias Knows
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confronts Gideon privately. She shows him one page; he goes pale recognizing an inspector's signature — his superior. He must choose: report her or join her. Beat: the alliance neither wanted.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over weeks of covert meetings, Gideon and Elias fall for each other while planning the final run past checkpoint three, the telegraph office. Both know exposure means prison — or the sea. Beat: love kindled inside danger.

chapters.title: Sefu Pays
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Sefu is arrested on trumped-up theft charges meant to make him talk. He says nothing and is shipped to a harsher station. Gideon's guilt doubles her determination. Beat: grief converted to fuel.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The company's auditor arrives early, burning loose records. The original ledger is now the only copy in existence — raising its value and its lethality. Beat: the clock starts ticking audibly.

chapters.title: Nell Taken
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The overseer, suspicious, takes Nell into the company house 'for care.' Gideon realizes they've deduced the child matters. Desperate, she considers trading the ledger for the girl. Beat: the theme made flesh — price of survival.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The company offers freedom papers in exchange for the ledger and silence. Gideon, remembering every name in its columns, refuses. Elias backs her, risking his career. Beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Wire
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax build. They plan to send ledger copies by telegraph to a Perth newspaper and carry the original to the magistrate through the telegraph office itself. The plan requires drawing every eye. Beat: coiled anticipation.

chapters.title: The Night Run
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Under cover of a cyclone warning, Gideon dives the old channel to bypass the road checkpoint, nearly drowns, and surfaces inside the town jetty pilings with the oilskin-wrapped book. Beat: terror and triumph in salt water.

chapters.title: Magistrate's Door
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias delivers the ledger to Magistrate Corrigan, who reveals he's been waiting years for such evidence but warns them: testimony will destroy them both. They swear it anyway. Beat: quiet, iron commitment.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the packed courtroom, Gideon reads names aloud from the ledger while company lawyers circle. Nell, held by the nun, is identified by a surviving aunt. The overseer breaks and implicates his superiors. Beat: catharsis — justice spoken outside the law's usual reach.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Ash
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The company collapses; contracts are voided. But Gideon loses her livelihood, her barracks, and any home here. Elias is dismissed from customs. They have won and are left with almost nothing. Beat: victory's bitter taste.

chapters.title: What Nell Calls Home
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon, Nell, and the freed divers pool wages to lease a small boat and begin independent pearl fishing. Sefu returns, thin but alive. Nell calls the boat 'home.' Beat: chosen family over given fate.

chapters.title: The Open Ledger
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, closing frame. Years later, Gideon keeps the ledger open on a shelf, not hidden — a record and a warning. She and Elias marry quietly; she teaches Nell to read the names first. Final line echoes chapter one: she counts her breaths, but now they are her own. Beat: peace earned, never given.
